title: Path (paths/items/<id>/path.json)
description: What a drive, an alley or a garden path is made of, as the house view lays it along a centre line. Either a surface, an unbroken strip whose texture is drawn from a few numbers, or modules, elements set one after another with the ground showing between them (stepping stones, landscape sleepers, log rounds).

kind.description: surface: one unbroken strip the width of the path. module: elements set one after another along its centre line, the ground showing between them.

draft.description: Colour of the path on the overlay of the editor, where it is drawn flat and bright rather than lit.

width.description: Width of the path in metres: the one it is given when chosen, and the bounds offered. A line of stepping stones is narrow, a drive is wide.

surface.description: An unbroken strip (kind: surface). Its texture is painted from these numbers alone, so a surface added to the catalog looks like itself without a line of code.

tile.description: Metres of path covered by one tile of the texture.

grain.description: Strength of the speckled noise over the base colour: 0 flat, 1 coarse.

speckles.description: Grains, chippings or pebbles scattered over the strip, drawn in the order given.

amount.description: Share of the strip they cover.

size.description: Size of one grain, in metres.

stretch.description: How many times longer than wide a grain is, turned any way: 1 a pebble, 4 a chip of bark or a shard of slate.

joints.description: Lines of mortar or sand between the units of a laid surface: pavers, slabs, bricks, decking boards.

cell.description: Size of one unit in metres: along the path, then across it. A decking board is long and narrow.

width.description: Width of a joint, in metres.

stagger.description: How far one row is set off from the next, as a share of a unit: 0 lines up, 0.5 is a running bond.

shade.description: How much the units differ in colour from one another: 0 all alike, 1 a patchwork.

wheels.description: Two tracks worn by wheels across the width, the surface colour showing between and beside them: a grass track with earth ruts. A surface that has them is painted across its whole width rather than repeated.

bands.description: Each track as the share of the width it covers, from one edge: [0.12, 0.36] is a rut a quarter of the way in.

speckles.description: Grains scattered over the tracks alone.

amount.description: Share of the strip they cover.

size.description: Size of one grain, in metres.

stretch.description: How many times longer than wide a grain is, turned any way: 1 a pebble, 4 a chip of bark or a shard of slate.

module.description: Elements set one after another along the centre line (kind: module), the ground showing between them. Their shape, size and colour are drawn at random between the bounds given, so no two elements of a path are quite alike.

shapes.description: Shapes the elements are taken from, one per element. round: a disc. half-moon: a disc cut straight on one side. slab: a rectangle with rounded corners (a landscape sleeper is a long one). oval: an ellipse. stone: an irregular slab, as a broken paving stone.

size.description: Size of one element in metres: along the path, then across it.

thickness.description: How far the element stands over the ground, in metres.

gap.description: Ground left between two elements, in metres. A stride is about 0.6 m from one stepping stone to the next.

colors.description: Colours the elements are taken from, one per element.

vary.description: How much the elements differ from one another.

size.description: Share of the size an element may gain or lose.

angle.description: How far an element may be turned off the line, in turns: 0.25 is a quarter turn either way.

side.description: How far an element may be set off the centre line, as a share of its width.

shade.description: How much an element may be lightened or darkened from the colour it was given.
